new_statements.rule_in_words: The only accessible phonological description of Kadaru (Kurtala clan dialect) treats prosody solely in terms of vowel length and (tentatively contrastive) lexical tone, with H vs L minimal pairs; it says nothing about word stress or accent placement. The sister dialect Tagle/Taglennaa (Ibrahim & Jakobi 2015: 193-194, file) is described first-hand with lexical and grammatical tone ('number is either solely marked by tonal contrast... or by tonal contrast combined with the alternation of the root vowel', e.g. ájɛ̀ / àjɛ́ 'wide'), again with no stress statement. Tucker & Bryan 1966: 314 (from Stevenson's MS notes) likewise report for Kadaru 'a few lexical tone doublets... there would seem to be three level tones' and give stress remarks only for Dongolawi and Fadicca. No source seen states where stress falls in Kadaru.
new_statements.secondary_stress: Nothing said in any source seen.
new_statements.exceptions: None; Alaki & Norton flag their tone evidence as tentative and note long vowels cluster in CV monosyllables (possible predictable lengthening).
new_statements.domain_note: Isolated citation forms (wordlist elicitation for an alphabet workshop); tone contrasts shown on mono- and disyllabic nouns. Tagle evidence (Ibrahim & Jakobi) concerns word-level lexical/grammatical tone on nouns, adjectives and suffixes.
new_statements.identity_note: Alaki & Norton 2015 describe the Kurtala (Ngokra) clan dialect of Kadaru [kdu], one of six mutually intelligible clan dialects of the 'Six Mountains' (Dabatna, Kafir, Kurtala, Kadaru/Kodur, Kuldaji, Kururu/Tagle). Ibrahim & Jakobi 2015, Gulfan 2015 and Ibrahim & Huttenga 2007 describe Tagle = Taglennaa = Kururu/Kororo, which Ethnologue and Glottolog (lgcode 'Tagle = Kadaru [kdu]') file under kada1282; no separate Glottolog languoid code was verified for Tagle. Meinhof 1918/19 'Kadero' and Stevenson's notes (via Tucker & Bryan 1966) refer to Kadaru proper (Kodur).

sources.note: Nothing on stress at all. Sec. C 'Syllables and prosody': C.1 syllable types; C.2 'Vowel length and tone' (pp.226-227) gives 'only tentative initial evidence' for vowel length and tone, Table 16 'Possible tone contrasts' (tɛ́ː grinding / tɛ̀ː lake, kál / kàl, kákáː / kàkà, ʊ́nɪ̀ / ʊ̀nɪ̀), 'More investigation is needed to be able to analyse tone'; conclusion (p.229) leaves prosodic analysis to others, pointing to Ibrahim & Huttenga 2007 on the Tagle dialect. Orthography recommended without tone marks.
